title: Ritual wine container (fangyi)
summary: This fangyi is an early Western Zhou bronze ritual wine vessel decorated with taotie masks, serpents, birds, and long cast inscriptions.
description: This exhibit is based on a Smithsonian 3D model of a ritual wine container, or fangyi, from early Western Zhou dynasty China, around 1100 BCE. The vessel is made of bronze and decorated with taotie mask patterns, serpents, birds, and layered relief ornament. It is especially important because it contains a long cast inscription of 187 characters, repeated inside both the vessel and the lid. The inscription records administrative meetings and ritual ceremonies held in Chengzhou during the reign of King Zhao, the fourth Zhou monarch. It also describes gifts of ritual wine, bronze, and oxen awarded for ritual use. In this exhibition, the fangyi can be introduced as an object where political authority, ancestral ritual, bronze casting, writing, and visual symbolism meet in one compact vessel.
sourceInstitution: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art
